title: Unique partial sorting permutation
statement: Let $n,a$ be natural numbers with $a\le n$, and let $\sigma$ be a permutation of $\mathrm{Fin}(n)$. There is exactly one permutation $\tau$ agreeing with $\sigma$ at every position $k<a$ and satisfying $\tau(i)<\tau(j)$ whenever $a\le i<j$. Both the empty prefix and the empty tail are allowed.

source.place: Tag 01FM, definition of sigma_a preceding cohomology-equation-first-homotopy

proof.text: Define the injective numerical key f(k)=sigma^{-1}(k) when sigma^{-1}(k)<a and f(k)=n+k otherwise. Apply Mathlib Tuple.sort to this key. By strong induction on k<a, the preimage of sigma(k) cannot precede k because earlier positions already agree with sigma. Monotonicity of the sorted key bounds its value at k by k. A smaller value would repeat an earlier prefix entry, so the value is k and the entry is sigma(k).

Beyond the prefix, sigma^{-1}(tau(i)) cannot lie below a, or bijectivity would repeat a fixed prefix label. Thus the key is n+tau(i), and its monotonicity plus injectivity gives a strictly increasing tail. Conversely every permutation satisfying the two filters orders the injective key: use prefix indices, the gap at n, and increasing labels in the three respective cases. Mathlib Tuple.eq_sort_iff identifies it with Tuple.sort f. The same argument covers n=0, a=0 and a=n.

lean.statement:
theorem cechPartialSort_existsUnique (n : ℕ) (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n))
    (a : ℕ) (_ha : a ≤ n) :
    ∃! τ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n),
      (∀ k, k.val < a → τ k = σ k) ∧
      (∀ i j, a ≤ i.val → i < j → τ i < τ j)
